4146.statement: A light dependant resistor (LDR) only senses light levels.
4146.correction: An LDR's resistance changes depending on the amount of light it is exposed to. As the light level increases, the resistance decreases. This change in resistance can create a voltage change, which can be used as a signal to control an output.

3887.belief: Iterations are only needed when a system doesn't work.
3887.statement: Iterations are only needed when a system doesn't work.
3887.correction: Systems are iterated to modify, fix, develop and improve.

2888.belief: Fabrics are always joined by stitching.
2888.statement: Fabrics are always joined by stitching.
2888.correction: Fabrics can be joined using stitching, adhesives and mechanical fixings.

5141.belief: Only one method of integrating the components in a control system is used.
5141.statement: Only one method of integrating the components in a control system is used.
5141.correction: Different methods of integrating components can be combined, depending on the device's function and features.

8693.belief: Quality is only considered when the product has been completed.
8693.statement: Quality is only considered when the product has been completed.
8693.correction: Quality is considered at all stages of manufacture.

2774.correction: Evaluating is most effective if it involves more than one person's opinion and data gathered from testing.

9377.belief: Smart materials are only for fun products like colour changing mugs!
9377.statement: Smart materials are only for fun products like colour changing mugs!
9377.correction: Smart materials give designers and engineers exciting possibilities when developing new products. Possibilities often focus on function and/or form. For example, thermochromic materials can be used to indicate a temperature and warn users of danger.

2296.belief: Designing is only creative when innovative ideas are produced.
2296.statement: Designing is only creative when innovative ideas are produced.
2296.correction: Designing is creative at every stage, not just when coming up with brand-new ideas. Creativity is also shown in solving problems, improving existing products, and making designs more user-friendly, sustainable, or affordable.

2863.belief: Exploring the context should happen quickly so that you can get to the most important phase of designing.
2863.statement: Exploring the context should happen quickly so that you can get to the most important phase of designing.
2863.correction: Designing is an important phase. However, taking the time to really explore the context and understand the users needs and wants will provide solid foundations for successful designing.

5834.belief: Product analysis leads to copying of designs.
5834.statement: Product analysis leads to copying of designs.
5834.correction: Product analysis identifies successful features and those which can be improved, this can lead to inspiration for new or improved ideas.

8812.belief: Redesigning and evolving existing products is not really designing and does not show any creativity or innovation.
8812.statement: Redesigning and evolving existing products is not really designing and does not show any creativity or innovation.
8812.correction: Redesigning existing products is a part of design work and often requires significant creativity, insight, and innovation. Some of the most impactful design breakthroughs came not from inventing something new, but from improving what already exists.

10676.belief: User feedback is just opinions, it’s not useful when developing designs.
10676.statement: User feedback is just opinions, it’s not useful when developing designs.
10676.correction: Feedback is largely based on opinions. However, it provides real world insight into how people interact see, understand and would use a design.

2286.belief: Design optimisation is the same as design development.
2286.statement: Design optimisation is the same as design development.
2286.correction: Design development is the bigger process of taking an idea and turning it into a final product. Optimisation is the specific part of development where you focus on preparing the design for making, creating the best version of your existing design.

11195.belief: When your final design has already been decided, it is a waste of time reflecting back on the design journey.
11195.statement: When your final design has already been decided, it is a waste of time reflecting back on the design journey.
11195.correction: Even though the final design may be decided, reflection is not about changing the outcome, it's about understanding how you got there, what you learned, and how you can improve in the future.

1669.correction: The circular economy can be defined as products and materials being kept in circulation and not becoming waste. Design decisions within circular economy can be generated through consideration of 6 Rs: recycle, reuse, rethink, refuse, repair, reduce.

2709.belief: Environmental impact only occurs when products are disposed of.
2709.statement: Environmental impact only occurs when products are disposed of.
2709.correction: Circular economy and LCA consider the environmental impact at every single stage of a product's life cycle.

10073.belief: Sustainability decisions happen after the product has been designed.
10073.statement: Sustainability decisions happen after the product has been designed.
10073.correction: At the design stage, designers have a huge responsibility to influence many other stages of a product's life cycle through their design decisions.

2707.belief: The only environmental decision at the manufacture and materials processing stage is the choice between renewable/non renewable sources of energy.
2707.statement: The only environmental decision at the manufacture and materials processing stage is the choice between renewable/non renewable sources of energy.
2707.correction: Environmental decisions include sources of energy, use of recycled materials, sustainable land management such as deforestation, pollution including water pollution and transportation. During manufacture, ethical impacts should also be considered.

10948.belief: The only way to reduce environmental impact at the distribution stage is through using electric vehicles.
10948.statement: The only way to reduce environmental impact at the distribution stage is through using electric vehicles.
10948.correction: There are many ways such as designing flat pack, stackable, lightweight products, and location of manufacture.

1993.belief: Considering a product's energy use is the only way to design a sustainable product.
1993.statement: Considering a product's energy use is the only way to design a sustainable product.
1993.correction: There are many other ways to design a product to be sustainable when in use, including designing products to grow with users, be adjusted, modular, reused etc.

8886.belief: Repair, maintenance and recycling is the sole responibility of the user.
8886.statement: Repair, maintenance and recycling is the sole responibility of the user.
8886.correction: Design decisions made at the design/redesign stage can determine the ease and ability of a product to be repaired, maintained and recycled.

8813.belief: Redesigning a product for the circular economy only means making it recyclable.
8813.statement: Redesigning a product for the circular economy only means making it recyclable.
8813.correction: Redesign in the circular economy involves designing products to last longer, be repaired, reused, or upgraded to reduce waste throughout the product’s entire life cycle.

5735.belief: Possible outcome design fixation limits context exploration. Product analysis leads to copying.
5735.statement: Possible outcome design fixation limits context exploration. Product analysis leads to copying.
5735.correction: Product analysis identifies successful features and those which can be improved.

10325.correction: Timber can be a sustainable material if sourced from a Forest Stewardship Council certified supplier. FSC forests are managed to strict environmental, social, and ecological standards.

5688.belief: All polymers are non biodegradable and can last for hundreds of year.
5688.statement: All polymers are non biodegradable and can last for hundreds of year.
5688.correction: Polymers come in many forms including biodegradable and bio-based polymers that will break down more easily in the environment.

8811.correction: Most metals, including aluminium and steel, can be repeatedly recycled without negatively impacting their properties.

2180.correction: Data is information and can be recorded using both numbers and words.

608.belief: It is often believed that focusing on form means sacrificing function, and vice versa. The assumption is that a product can't be both beautiful and functional.
608.statement: It is often believed that focusing on form means sacrificing function, and vice versa. The assumption is that a product can't be both beautiful and functional.
608.correction: Good design brings together both form and function. The form of a product can enhance the function of a product by making it more enjoyable to use.

210.belief: Alessi is often thought of as a single designer.
210.statement: Alessi is often thought of as a single designer.
210.correction: Alessi is a group of designers.

2299.belief: Designing products using the average measurements in an anthropometric data set will provide a successful user experience for all users.
2299.statement: Designing products using the average measurements in an anthropometric data set will provide a successful user experience for all users.
2299.correction: Designing for the average person can diminish user experience and exclude a significant portion of the population from using products.

37.belief: 3D sketching is just 2D sketching with an additional dimension.
37.statement: 3D sketching is just 2D sketching with an additional dimension.
37.correction: To be able to sketch in 3D, we need to understand depth and perspective.

8878.correction: Rendering should consider tone and depth but also the texture of the material the product is made out of.

315.belief: Annotations can replace the need for a clear and accurate sketch.
315.statement: Annotations can replace the need for a clear and accurate sketch.
315.correction: Annotation provides further explanation or clarification on what is not visible in the sketch.

10106.belief: Systems are simple with just one input, process and output.
10106.statement: Systems are simple with just one input, process and output.
10106.correction: Systems can be complex with multiple inputs, processes and outputs, feedback and variables.

10107.correction: Systems often have multiple inputs. These can be switches and sensors.

4091.correction: LEDs can be grouped in strips or matrices to create patterns or messages.

783.belief: Buzzers all work in the same way.
783.statement: Buzzers all work in the same way.
783.correction: Different buzzers work in different ways.

4729.belief: All motors operate in the same way.
4729.statement: All motors operate in the same way.
4729.correction: DC motors use open-loop systems, and servo motors use a closed-loop system.

10783.belief: A variable is a set piece of data that can not change once collected.
10783.statement: A variable is a set piece of data that can not change once collected.
10783.correction: A variable is a named piece of data stored in a computer’s memory, accessed and changed by a computer program.

9178.belief: When we select a component, they are all the same.
9178.statement: When we select a component, they are all the same.
9178.correction: Different circuits and control systems require different value components. Changing one will affect the others.

10190.belief: Testing must always be done using a physical control system.
10190.statement: Testing must always be done using a physical control system.
10190.correction: Testing a control system can be done using a physical control system and a multimeter or using a CAD simulation.

791.belief: All CAD modelling is the same, whether working in Tinkercad or Fusion.
791.statement: All CAD modelling is the same, whether working in Tinkercad or Fusion.
791.correction: Different CAD applications work in three distinct ways, constructive solid geometry, solid modelling and parametric modelling.

5507.belief: Physical sketching is the same as sketching in parametric CAD.
5507.statement: Physical sketching is the same as sketching in parametric CAD.
5507.correction: Sketches in parametric CAD need to be constrained in order to create accurate and error free models.

9359.belief: A sketch is always needed to be able to use the Extrude command in Fusion.
9359.statement: A sketch is always needed to be able to use the Extrude command in Fusion.
9359.correction: Users can extrude from component faces and existing solid bodies.

35.belief: 3D printing is sustainable because it is an additive manufacturing process with minimal waste.
35.statement: 3D printing is sustainable because it is an additive manufacturing process with minimal waste.
35.correction: 3D printing filament is a thermopolymer. As with all manufacturing processes, there needs to be consideration of the materials used, their sources and disposal.

119.belief: Adding physical materials to components in Fusion is for aesthetic purposes only.
119.statement: Adding physical materials to components in Fusion is for aesthetic purposes only.
119.correction: Adding physical materials to components alters their appearance and properties.

1873.belief: Components can be placed by eye when assembly modelling in Fusion.
1873.statement: Components can be placed by eye when assembly modelling in Fusion.
1873.correction: To create assemblies in Fusion, the correct joints should be used to replicate how components are assembled in the real world.

10159.belief: Technical drawings created in CAD are always correct and error-free.
10159.statement: Technical drawings created in CAD are always correct and error-free.
10159.correction: Using CAD reduces human error; however, users must add correct and relevant dimensions. Incorrect constraints can also result in errors.

10192.belief: Testing only happens when the final prototype has been made.
10192.statement: Testing only happens when the final prototype has been made.
10192.correction: Testing should happen throughout the iterative journey, so that design decisions are made to meet design requirements and produce a successful design solution.

670.belief: Biomimicry is using nature to inspire aesthetics.
670.statement: Biomimicry is using nature to inspire aesthetics.
670.correction: Biomimicry uses nature to inspire solutions to problems, biomorphism is about nature inspiring aesthetics.

2705.belief: Envionmental impact can only be assessed after a product has been manufactured.
2705.statement: Envionmental impact can only be assessed after a product has been manufactured.
2705.correction: Environmental impact can be assessed at every and all stages of the iterative design process.

9548.belief: All specifications must use the same subheadings.
9548.statement: All specifications must use the same subheadings.
9548.correction: Specifications must be specific to the context, design opportunity and design brief.

3799.belief: Innovation has to be revolutionary and entirely original.
3799.statement: Innovation has to be revolutionary and entirely original.
3799.correction: Innovation can be revolutinary like the 'cats eye' or evolutionary where ideas change gradually and evolve over time.

10740.belief: Using sources of inspiration when designing is copying.
10740.statement: Using sources of inspiration when designing is copying.
10740.correction: When using sources of inspiration, they are usually not solutions or similar products but instead any image or product that inspires a spark of creativity.

2314.belief: Development of design ideas is coming up with a completely new idea or the idea has to be changed significantly.
2314.statement: Development of design ideas is coming up with a completely new idea or the idea has to be changed significantly.
2314.correction: Developing an idea can be changing and altering very small things such as function, materials, size, proportion or aesthetics.

10685.belief: Using AI when designing is cheating.
10685.statement: Using AI when designing is cheating.
10685.correction: AI can be used to help inspire us and is used to develop our own ideas. We must just be open and honest in our use of it.

5901.belief: All prototypes must be life size.
5901.statement: All prototypes must be life size.
5901.correction: It is not always possible to manufacture life size prototypes. The space to manufacture and store may be limited plus the materials may be expensive. A smaller scale product saves space and materials but still allows for a product to be manufactured.

1646.belief: Choosing materials is always based on aesthetics.
1646.statement: Choosing materials is always based on aesthetics.
1646.correction: Many factors determine the material choice, such as the purpose and environment of the product. For example, cotton calico is absorbent and not suitable for damp or humid places unless finished with a waterproof layer.

5249.belief: Orthographic projections are completed after manufacture.
5249.statement: Orthographic projections are completed after manufacture.
5249.correction: Orthographic projections are known as a working drawing. These are sent from a designer to a manufacturer before manufacturing to enable them to manufacture the product or component.

5346.belief: Parts lists are only needed for materials or components which need to be bought in.
5346.statement: Parts lists are only needed for materials or components which need to be bought in.
5346.correction: A parts lists supports the thinking needed in preparation of manufacture for all components of a design. They help identify quantities and can highlight mistakes. A well-structured parts list speeds up production and ensures cost efficiency.

3213.belief: Gantt charts are used to plan out the whole design project.
3213.statement: Gantt charts are used to plan out the whole design project.
3213.correction: Gantt charts can be used as a tool to plan out the whole design project. However it can be beneficial to use Gantt charts for the individual phases within the project, like the manufacturing stage. This can improve efficiency at crucial stages.

4468.belief: Any marking tool will work on any material.
4468.statement: Any marking tool will work on any material.
4468.correction: Using the wrong tool (e.g a pencil on metal) can result in unclear or inaccurate marks. Different materials require specific marking tools, such as pencils for paper and boards and marking knives for wood.

5754.belief: Practice using the tools is not needed when working with textiles and timbers as they are easy to cut.
5754.statement: Practice using the tools is not needed when working with textiles and timbers as they are easy to cut.
5754.correction: Practice is needed when using tools to cut all materials. Textiles and timbers are easy to cut, but complete control can be lost if cut too quickly. It can be challenging to keep on the line, so practice is needed.

10712.belief: Using machinery results in greater accuracy.
10712.statement: Using machinery results in greater accuracy.
10712.correction: Machinery or hand tools can result in accurate manufacturing. Accuracy is achieved with careful planning and execution with skill.

8695.belief: Quality control checks are performed on products after they are made to ensure they meet the required quality standards for sale or use.
8695.statement: Quality control checks are performed on products after they are made to ensure they meet the required quality standards for sale or use.
8695.correction: Quality control checks are performed throughout the process to ensure quality remains constant.

22.belief: Only 2-dimensional products can be manufactured using a laser cutter.
22.statement: Only 2-dimensional products can be manufactured using a laser cutter.
22.correction: Lamination can be used to create more curved and organic shapes or to create strength in an object.

3853.belief: When investigating a context, you should only consider the user's preferences.
3853.statement: When investigating a context, you should only consider the user's preferences.
3853.correction: Within a context, there are different groups of people who have different preferences. It is important for designers to consider these groups and their different social and cultural backgrounds, as well environmental considerations.

3040.belief: Fixating on one idea or existing ideas will lead to innovative designing.
3040.statement: Fixating on one idea or existing ideas will lead to innovative designing.
3040.correction: Design fixation is the opposite of being innovative and is focussing or fixating on one idea or existing ideas. This can limit creativity and innovation.

10690.belief: Using closed questions in an interview will provide enough effective information to support further developments.
10690.statement: Using closed questions in an interview will provide enough effective information to support further developments.
10690.correction: Using open-ended questions in an interview will allow for more detailed and flexible reponses, providing oppotunites for effective outcomes to support further developments.

8710.belief: Questionnaires are only used to present data in graphs when investigating a context.
8710.statement: Questionnaires are only used to present data in graphs when investigating a context.
8710.correction: Questionnaires inform designing and provide evidence to justify design decisions.

2183.belief: All data can be presented as a graph or chart.
2183.statement: All data can be presented as a graph or chart.
2183.correction: The way in which data is presented will depend on whether the data is quantitative or qualitative.

5737.belief: It is only possible to present quantitative data.
5737.statement: It is only possible to present quantitative data.
5737.correction: Qualitative data can be presented in other formats to summarise findings.

5364.belief: Patents and trademarks are the same thing.
5364.statement: Patents and trademarks are the same thing.
5364.correction: Trademarks protect brand names and logos whilst patents protect inventions and new technologies.

723.belief: Branding and logos are the same thing.
723.statement: Branding and logos are the same thing.
723.correction: Branding is the way of making a company’s product or service more visible and recognisable. A logo is just a small part of branding and is a simple symbol or design that represents a business or brand.

9395.belief: Socioeconomic status is just about a person's income.
9395.statement: Socioeconomic status is just about a person's income.
9395.correction: It is a combination of things such as income, education, occupation and even influence.

2276.belief: A design brief should be very specific and identify a product that will be designed and manufactured.
2276.statement: A design brief should be very specific and identify a product that will be designed and manufactured.
2276.correction: To avoid design fixation, a design brief should be non-specific and open. A design brief should focus on the context and the problem, and not name a product that will be designed and made.

6196.statement: Pupils may come with an idea or even a solution at this stage and stick with it as they feel they do not need another idea.
6196.correction: Encourage pupils to explore a range of ideas and possibilities to avoid design fixation and prepare them for the NEA.

8905.belief: Research into existing products is a secondary research task.
8905.statement: Research into existing products is a secondary research task.
8905.correction: Primary research through the disassembly of a product can be extremely beneficial to really understand a product, its materials and how it is manufactured.

10741.belief: Using standardised components limit creativity and originality in design.
10741.statement: Using standardised components limit creativity and originality in design.
10741.correction: Standardised components can actually enhance innovation by allowing designers to focus on customisation, functionality, and efficiency while reducing costs and production time.

4137.belief: The life cycle in product design ends once the product is sold to the consumer.
4137.statement: The life cycle in product design ends once the product is sold to the consumer.
4137.correction: The product life cycle includes stages beyond purchase such as: use, maintenance, and disposal or recycling. Sustainable design considers the entire life cycle to minimise environmental impact.

7577.statement: Pupils tend to define a product that they wish to design and make at this point. They become fixated on a design.
7577.correction: Pupils need to keep their design brief open so that it does not create design fixation.

2284.belief: Design ideas are produced through sketches and drawings.
2284.statement: Design ideas are produced through sketches and drawings.
2284.correction: 3D or physical modelling is a great way to get design ideas out of your head. It is sometimes easier to work out your idea in 3D rather than worrying about whether you can draw it in 3D, especially if its form is complex.

3886.belief: Iterations of models are purely based on the thoughts of the designer.
3886.statement: Iterations of models are purely based on the thoughts of the designer.
3886.correction: Iterations can be based off a range of analysis and evaluations such as evaluating against the users needs and wants as well as direct feedback from the user.

4695.belief: Modelling only takes place with physical materials.
4695.statement: Modelling only takes place with physical materials.
4695.correction: Virtual modelling using 3D drawing software can help to see ideas in 3D and enables quick and easy iteration.

4696.belief: Modelling using CAD is the final step in the development of designs.
4696.statement: Modelling using CAD is the final step in the development of designs.
4696.correction: CAD is part of the iterative process. CAD should be used as a way to develop your idea by viewing it virtually and analysing the idea. Sketching over your CAD drawings can help to develop the idea before going back to make those improvements in CAD.

5079.belief: Once a design has been decided upon, it cannot be altered.
5079.statement: Once a design has been decided upon, it cannot be altered.
5079.correction: A design can continue to be altered, even when at the manufacturing stage.

4040.belief: Laser cutting is about cutting out simple shapes and only really works for 2D products and designs.
4040.statement: Laser cutting is about cutting out simple shapes and only really works for 2D products and designs.
4040.correction: Laser cutters can be used to develop and manufacture effective and complex 3D products.

3443.belief: Hand tools are outdated and less accurate than power tools.
3443.statement: Hand tools are outdated and less accurate than power tools.
3443.correction: Hand tools offer high precision when used correctly, especially for detailed work.

10711.belief: Using machinery to manufacture requires little skill when compared to using hand tools.
10711.statement: Using machinery to manufacture requires little skill when compared to using hand tools.
10711.correction: Using machinery to manufacture products takes skill and effort to achieve a high quaility finish, much like using hand tools.

8697.belief: Quality control and quality assurance is the same thing.
8697.statement: Quality control and quality assurance is the same thing.
8697.correction: Quality control focuses on identifying defects in finished products, while quality assurance is about preventing defects through planned processes and systems during production.

10324.belief: Timbers need a varnish to protect them.
10324.statement: Timbers need a varnish to protect them.
10324.correction: There are many different options to finish the surface of timber and these are chosen depending on the type of timber, intended use, planned aesthetics etc.

1780.belief: Commercial viability only relates to how well a product works.
1780.statement: Commercial viability only relates to how well a product works.
1780.correction: A product can work well or be aesthetically pleasing, but if it’s too expensive to make, doesn’t meet market demand, or won’t sell at a profit, it isn’t commercially viable.

2983.belief: The final evaluation is based upon the designers perspective of the prototype and design process.
2983.statement: The final evaluation is based upon the designers perspective of the prototype and design process.
2983.correction: Testing and evaluations from the user and target market are essential to ensure the product meets the clients needs but is also commercially viable.

2287.belief: A design portfolio should only include your best work and your best ideas.
2287.statement: A design portfolio should only include your best work and your best ideas.
2287.correction: A design portfolio should show the journey of the designer, including all of the ideas that were not taken through or were not successful.

4486.belief: All materials have additional surface finishes applied.
4486.statement: All materials have additional surface finishes applied.
4486.correction: Some materials, such as polymers, can be self-finishing and do not require additional processes or finishes.

3697.belief: Inclusive design and accessible design are the same thing.
3697.statement: Inclusive design and accessible design are the same thing.
3697.correction: Accessible design is about making sure people with disabilities can use something. Inclusive design is about making sure everyone can use it, by thinking about all kinds of differences, including mental health and wellbeing.

4568.belief: Mental health and wellbeing challenges are too personal or 'invisible' to be designed for.
4568.statement: Mental health and wellbeing challenges are too personal or 'invisible' to be designed for.
4568.correction: Designers don’t solve mental health itself, but create supportive products, services, or environments that ease challenges.

2639.belief: Empathy just means “feeling sorry” for others.
2639.statement: Empathy just means “feeling sorry” for others.
2639.correction: Empathy is understanding someone’s perspective and experience to inform design.

8904.correction: Designers critically analyse existing solutions to understand strengths/weaknesses for inspiration of new ideas.

3026.belief: The first idea is always the best.
3026.statement: The first idea is always the best.
3026.correction: Creativity improves with divergent thinking and iteration - the first idea is rarely the final one.

178.belief: The most aesthetically-pleasing idea is the best.
178.statement: The most aesthetically-pleasing idea is the best.
178.correction: Strong design choices balance creativity with inclusivity, feasibility, and impact - aesthetics alone aren’t enough.

5902.belief: Prototypes must be polished or look like the final product.
5902.statement: Prototypes must be polished or look like the final product.
5902.correction: Early prototypes are rough and quick - their purpose is to test ideas, not show perfection.

10196.belief: Testing is only to prove that a design works.
10196.statement: Testing is only to prove that a design works.
10196.correction: Testing is equally about finding flaws and learning what doesn’t work; failures provide insight.

8824.belief: Refinement is just “making it look nicer.”.
8824.statement: Refinement is just “making it look nicer.”
8824.correction: Refinement is purposeful change based on evidence; it improves inclusivity, usability, and overall function, not just appearance.

4542.belief: Medium-fidelity prototypes are just “tidier” versions of low-fidelity ones.
4542.statement: Medium-fidelity prototypes are just “tidier” versions of low-fidelity ones.
4542.correction: Medium-fidelity is not about neatness - it’s about using stronger materials and semi-functional builds to test ergonomics and usability.

10195.belief: Testing is a one-off activity that only happens at the end of designing.
10195.statement: Testing is a one-off activity that only happens at the end of designing.
10195.correction: Testing is an iterative process - it happens throughout development. Each round of testing reveals new insights and informs further refinement.

3480.belief: High-fidelity prototypes are only about appearance and surface finish.
3480.statement: High-fidelity prototypes are only about appearance and surface finish.
3480.correction: High-fidelity prototypes are about realism in both look and function. They should operate as closely as possible to the intended product - or convincingly simulate that functionality.

5898.belief: If a prototype works, it can definitely be manufactured successfully.
5898.statement: If a prototype works, it can definitely be manufactured successfully.
5898.correction: Functionality doesn’t guarantee feasibility or success. A design might work in one-off form but fail in cost, scale, or sustainability when made commercially.

3698.belief: Inclusive design only applies to disability or accessibility-related products.
3698.statement: Inclusive design only applies to disability or accessibility-related products.
3698.correction: Inclusive design applies to everyone. It’s about designing for human diversity - age, ability, background, culture, and mental wellbeing - across all industries.

9957.statement: Students often 'think' they understand a context without having fully explored it.
9957.correction: Students need to be encouraged to fully explore a context so to understand it fully before moving onto designing. This is great practice for the NEA.

2915.belief: Fairtrade is just the label on bananas.
2915.statement: Fairtrade is just the label on bananas.
2915.correction: Fairtrade is a system that ensures farmers and workers receive fair prices, decent working conditions and support for sustainable community development through trade.

8887.belief: Repair, maintenance and recycling is the sole responsibility of the user.
8887.statement: Repair, maintenance and recycling is the sole responsibility of the user.
8887.correction: Design decisions made at the design/redesign stage can determine the ease and ability of a product to be repaired, maintained and recycled.

4935.belief: New and emerging technologies have only positive impacts.
4935.statement: New and emerging technologies have only positive impacts.
4935.correction: New and emerging technologies can make some products obsolete. It can also mean that many workers with limited skills lose their jobs to robots. These workers may find it difficult, or may not want to, retrain.

4939.belief: All new technology is good and we should use it.
4939.statement: All new technology is good and we should use it.
4939.correction: New technology can be good but may also have negative consequences which responsible designers must consider.

8884.belief: Renewable sources of energy do not have any negative impacts.
8884.statement: Renewable sources of energy do not have any negative impacts.
8884.correction: Renewable sources of energy have high initial set up costs, are often weather dependent and require effective storage of energy.

1874.belief: Components all work however they are positioned in a circuit.
1874.statement: Components all work however they are positioned in a circuit.
1874.correction: Some components are polarised and only work if they are the correct way round.

2029.belief: Control systems are programmed with text-based languages.
2029.statement: Control systems are programmed with text-based languages.
2029.correction: Control systems can be programmed using different languages including text, blocks or flow charts.

4033.belief: The larger the diameter of a pulley wheel, the higher the output speed.
4033.statement: The larger the diameter of a pulley wheel, the higher the output speed.
4033.correction: The smaller the pulley wheel, the quicker it will complete a rotation, therefore increasing the output speed.

3728.belief: Increasing the size of the driven gear, increases the output speed.
3728.statement: Increasing the size of the driven gear, increases the output speed.
3728.correction: Decreasing the size of the driven gear (or increasing the size of driver gear), increases the speed of the driven gear.

10209.belief: Textiles are not made from fossil fuels.
10209.statement: Textiles are not made from fossil fuels.
10209.correction: Synthetic fibres are usually made from fossil fuels such a polyester and ripstop nylon.

4489.belief: A material's properties are fixed and cannot be changed.
4489.statement: A material's properties are fixed and cannot be changed.
4489.correction: Many materials can be altered after they are made to improve their properties, e.g. strength.

4490.belief: All materials are ready to use in their natural state.
4490.statement: All materials are ready to use in their natural state.
4490.correction: Raw materials need to go through a range of processing stages to make them usable.

9077.belief: The same tools and methods are used for both small-scale and industrial manufacturing.
9077.statement: The same tools and methods are used for both small-scale and industrial manufacturing.
9077.correction: The scale of production heavily influences tool choice, speed, accuracy, and repeatability.

3923.belief: All joining methods work the same for every material.
3923.statement: All joining methods work the same for every material.
3923.correction: Different materials need different joining methods based on their properties.

4478.belief: Mass production and continuous production are the same thing.
4478.statement: Mass production and continuous production are the same thing.
4478.correction: Mass production stops and starts, but continuous production never stops.

4731.belief: A mould and a former are the same thing.
4731.statement: A mould and a former are the same thing.
4731.correction: A mould contains the material and shapes it as it sets or solidifies. A former is a shape around which a material is bent or stretched.

8696.belief: Quality control is only about looking at the product at the very end of production.
8696.statement: Quality control is only about looking at the product at the very end of production.
8696.correction: Quality Control can happen throughout production (in-process checks, sampling, functional tests), not just at the end.

8903.belief: Research is only conducted at the beginning of a project.
8903.statement: Research is only conducted at the beginning of a project.
8903.correction: Research is involved in several stages of the design process.

5833.belief: Product analysis is only about identifying flaws or problems in a product.
5833.statement: Product analysis is only about identifying flaws or problems in a product.
5833.correction: In reality, product analysis is used to improve design, meet user needs, and stay competitive.

2277.belief: Design briefs are only used in creative fields like product or graphic design.
2277.statement: Design briefs are only used in creative fields like product or graphic design.
2277.correction: Design briefs are crucial across many industries, including engineering, architecture, and product development.

2289.belief: Design specifications and technical specifications are the same.
2289.statement: Design specifications and technical specifications are the same.
2289.correction: Design specifications focus on the overall concept, user needs, and appearance. Technical specifications detail the materials and measurement requirements needed to build a product.

2057.belief: The cost of a product only concerns raw materials.
2057.statement: The cost of a product only concerns raw materials.
2057.correction: Other factors like labour, overhead, distribution, and economies of scale affect the cost of a product.

4412.belief: Manufacturing process selection is solely based on cost.
4412.statement: Manufacturing process selection is solely based on cost.
4412.correction: Factors like product complexity, material properties, production volume, and lead time also play crucial roles.

5836.belief: Product safety is only about consumer protection.
5836.statement: Product safety is only about consumer protection.
5836.correction: Industry safety also includes protecting workers.

8686.belief: QA and QC are the same thing.
8686.statement: QA and QC are the same thing.
8686.correction: QA (Quality Assurance) focuses on preventing defects by improving the production process, while QC (Quality Control) focuses on identifying and fixing defects in the finished product.

2899.belief: Factories always produce goods in large amounts.
2899.statement: Factories always produce goods in large amounts.
2899.correction: Factories are responsive and often adjust production methods based on demand.

2951.belief: Feedback is only used to fix problems.
2951.statement: Feedback is only used to fix problems.
2951.correction: Industries use feedback not just to solve issues but also to innovate, improve efficiency, enhance customer satisfaction, and stay competitive.

3771.belief: Industries only modify products to make them cheaper.
3771.statement: Industries only modify products to make them cheaper.
3771.correction: Industries also improve products for better performance, sustainability, customer satisfaction, safety and compliance with regulations.

8039.belief: They need to know what they are designing and making straight away.
8039.statement: Pupils often think they need to know what they are designing and making straight away.
8039.correction: Pupils need to explore the context fully first to identify lots of possible design problems to solve before narrowing it down.

6869.statement: Pupils will know who their primary user is and will want to start designing.
6869.correction: Pupils need to find out more about the primary user and stakeholders so that they can define suitable and researched design requirements. This subsequently leads to successful design solutions.

8908.belief: Research only needs to take place at the start of the iterative design process.
8908.statement: Research only needs to take place at the start of the iterative design process.
8908.correction: Research is vital throughout the iterative design process and is not a linear activity. Pupils can research at any point to aid their design decisions and provide inspiration throughout the iterative process.

9547.belief: A specification is written after research and then referred to once the product is manufactured.
9547.statement: A specification is written after research and then referred to once the product is manufactured.
9547.correction: Design requirements should be used throughout the iterative journey (not just at the end!) to test concepts and make effective design decisions to creatively develop the product into a successful design.

9363.belief: Sketching is the only way to iterate design ideas.
9363.statement: Sketching is the only way to iterate design ideas.
9363.correction: Design ideas and iterations can be communicated using various techniques, such as sketching, CAD, prototyping, and AI.

10307.belief: Three design ideas are enough to avoid design fixation.
10307.statement: Three design ideas are enough to avoid design fixation.
10307.correction: There are many ways to generate design ideas that avoid design fixation and produce a range of successful ideas that pupils can develop on their iterative journey.

5954.statement: Pupils often already know what they want to design and feel that their first prototype is the final solution that doesn't need further development.
5954.correction: The iterative journey transforms an idea into a successful product. Pupils should carefully explore, experiment, test, and develop ideas while keeping design requirements central to the process.

5985.belief: They know how to manufacture their design without the need for a manufacturing specification.
5985.statement: Some pupils will assume that they know how to manufacture their design without the need for a manufacturing specification.
5985.correction: Designs are rarely understood by verbal explanation, they need visual representations with specific details of materials, dimensions, finishes and suitable processes. Communication methods will vary depending on your design.

8598.statement: Pupils will use only their manufacturing specification when making.
8598.correction: Many pupils will struggle with time managment when manufacturing. Pupils need to plan out their time so that they can keep on track to meet their deadline whilst thinking about the operational elements.

9680.statement: Students become so busy manufacturing their design solution that they often forget to evidence their manufacture.
9680.correction: It's easy to overlook the effort behind a product from the final photo. Documenting the manufacturing process highlights the skills, techniques, safety, and quality checks students use, proving their work, not the technician's.

4706.belief: Modifications are often quickly generated by the student's personal opinions, rather than their evaluations.
4706.statement: Modifications are often quickly generated by the student's personal opinions, rather than their evaluations.
4706.correction: Modifications should be informed from thorough testing and evaluation against design requirements with feedback from the primary user/stakeholders/experts.
